title: Planner: task hierarchy (nested tasks) in unified plans
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap target and distinguishes existing premium-plan licensing from unpublished unified-plan eligibility. The documented controls and beta API properties check out; targeted searches found no separate hierarchy switch or published rollout default.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to introduce nested tasks in Planner unified plans.
claims.quote: Task Hierarchy for Unified Plans in Planner introduces nested tasks to organize complex work, making plan structure clearer and execution easier.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes clearer plan structure and easier execution as the purpose of nested tasks.
claims.quote: introduces nested tasks to organize complex work, making plan structure clearer and execution easier.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published which licences will permit creating nested tasks, or the view-only split, in unified plans.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner task hierarchy unified plans licensing. Read Planner for admins, the service description, the beta task resource and Planner plans and pricing. Published hierarchy entitlements are qualified as premium-plan capabilities, not the forthcoming unified-plan split.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published
claims.claim: No per-user price specific to this feature beyond existing Planner subscriptions has been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner task hierarchy unified default licensing price meter; Planner task hierarchy meter pricing. Read the service description, Planner for admins and Microsoft Planner plans and pricing; found subscription prices but no separate unified-plan hierarchy price.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no meter specifically for task hierarchy.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner task hierarchy meter pricing; Planner task hierarchy nested tasks unified plans metered APIs pricing billing. Read the service description, beta task resource and Planner pricing. The general note that some Planner APIs are metered identifies no hierarchy meter.

claims.claim: Basic plans are now unified plans.
claims.quote: Basic plans are now unified plans.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Change & support; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Capabilities in a unified plan depend on each user's assigned licence, including additional capabilities from Copilot, Plan 1 or Plan 3.
claims.quote: Additional capabilities in unified plans are available based on whether the user has Microsoft Copilot, Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3.

claims.claim: Users with an eligible Microsoft 365 licence can create and work with unified plans.
claims.quote: Users with an eligible Microsoft 365 license can create and work with unified plans.

claims.claim: Unified plans are available to users with Microsoft 365, Planner Plan 1, Planner and Project Plan 3, or Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: All users with Microsoft 365, Planner Plan 1, Planner and Project Plan 3, or Microsoft 365 Copilot can use unified plans.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Members can collaborate in the same unified plan without holding the same licence.
claims.quote: A unified plan doesn't require every member of the plan to have the same license. Users can collaborate in the same plan, while the capabilities available to each user depend on their assigned license.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The beta unified plans Graph task resource documents parentTaskId as the parent identifier of a subtask.
claims.quote:
A task in the Planner Unified plans Graph API.
| parentTaskId | String | ID of the parent task, if this task is a subtask. |

claims.claim: The beta task resource has a read-only hasChildren flag indicating subtasks.
claims.quote: | hasChildren | Boolean | Indicates whether the task has subtasks. Read-only. |

claims.claim: Microsoft does not support production use of the beta Graph API.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The unified task resource page contrasts its model with the basic plans API's plannerTask and plannerTaskDetails split.
claims.quote: Unlike the plannerTask/plannerTaskDetails split in the Planner Basic plans Graph API, a task in the Planner Unified plans Graph API has no separate details object

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[2].governs; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A user with a Planner premium licence can convert an eligible basic plan to a premium plan to obtain advanced capabilities such as subtasks.
claims.quote: Premium users can now add advanced features (Timeline view, dependencies, subtasks, etc.) to their plans by converting basic plans into premium plans that support those features.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 users have view-only access to premium capabilities outside their licence in premium plans.
claims.quote: In premium plans, Microsoft 365 users can use the capabilities included with their license and have view-only access to all other premium capabilities.

claims.claim: The sources do not state that this hierarchy release changes existing plans or tasks.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner unified plans nested subtasks task hierarchy rollout existing plans permissions sharing autonomous data. Read the roadmap, Planner for admins and beta task resource; none describes an existing-plan migration for this item.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Planner plans and their tasks remain within container-defined membership and visibility boundaries.
claims.quote: Within Planner, each Plan is inside a container, and access to the plan is defined by the container. For example, if the Plan is inside a Modern Group, then the members of the Group can see the contents of the Plan.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described new data access or sharing introduced by task hierarchy.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner unified plans nested subtasks task hierarchy rollout existing plans permissions sharing autonomous data. Read the roadmap, Planner security/privacy/compliance, Planner for admins and beta task resource; found no new data-access or sharing rule attributed to hierarchy.

claims.claim: The Planner Purview page supports eDiscovery content search and legal hold for tasks in plans shared with groups.
claims.quote:
eDiscovery content search and legal hold.
Supported Planner content: Tasks in Plans that are shared with groups.
Includes Tasks, comments, and attachments.

claims.claim: The Planner Purview page lists premium plans as unsupported.
claims.quote: Unsupported: Personal (roster) plans, plans in Loop components, premium plans (formerly projects), Shared and Private channel Plans (LWG backed Plans).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The Planner Purview page does not name unified plans or nested tasks, or describe preserving their parent-child structure.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner unified plans nested subtasks task hierarchy rollout existing plans permissions sharing autonomous data. Read the full Planner support in Microsoft Purview page: it names group-shared tasks and exclusions but not unified plans, nested tasks or parent-child preservation.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described a new identity, permission or sharing model introduced by nested tasks.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner unified plans nested subtasks task hierarchy rollout existing plans permissions sharing autonomous data. Read Planner security/privacy/compliance, Planner for admins, the roadmap and beta task resource; none describes a new identity or permission model for hierarchy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described autonomous actions introduced by task hierarchy.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner nested tasks permissions autonomous existing plans rollout. Read the roadmap, beta task resource, Planner for admins and Planner Agent documentation; no hierarchy-specific autonomous action was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Task hierarchy organises tasks within plans rather than describing an agent-execution capability.
claims.quote: Task Hierarchy for Unified Plans in Planner introduces nested tasks to organize complex work, making plan structure clearer and execution easier.

claims.claim: Users can start a 30-day Planner and Project Plan 3 trial from prompts within Planner.
claims.quote: When users follow the prompts in planner to enable a 30-day trial, they gain access to all the features and functionality available with a subscription license for Planner and Project Plan 3.

claims.claim: At the end of the trial, users can request a Planner and Project Plan 3 licence from their administrator.
claims.quote: At the end of the 30-day trial, they can request a Planner and Project Plan 3 license from their Microsoft 365 administrator.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses is the route to a user's licence assignments.
claims.quote:
go to the Users > Active users page.
Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to.
In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps.
Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a selected SKU using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least a License or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: No separate admin-centre setting or Set-PlannerConfiguration parameter for task hierarchy in unified plans is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner task hierarchy Set-PlannerConfiguration; Planner nested tasks default enable switch. Read Planner admin and tenant-setting pages for availability, conversion, calendar, rosters, channels, notifications and Agent; no hierarchy switch found.

claims.claim: No admin UI equivalent to the AllowDataFlowToDataverse tenant conversion switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner AllowDataFlowToDataverse admin center setting UI disable plan conversion. Read Disable the conversion of basic plans by users into premium plans and Converting basic plans into premium plans; the tenant switch is PowerShell-only in these results.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowDataFlowToDataverse $false disables users' conversion of basic plans into premium plans.
claims.quote:
run the following command to disable the conversion of basic plans to premium plan by users (it's enabled by default):
Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowDataFlowToDataverse $false

claims.claim: Basic-to-premium plan conversion is enabled by default.
claims.quote: disable the conversion of basic plans to premium plan by users (it's enabled by default)

claims.claim: AllowDataFlowToDataverse controls conversion to premium plans, not task hierarchy inside unified plans.
claims.quote: The AllowDataFlowToDataverse value returned by this command indicates whether users can convert basic plans.

claims.claim: No admin UI equivalent to the IsPlannerAllowed tenant-wide switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner IsPlannerAllowed tenant disable organization admin center UI. Read Turn off Planner for your organization and admin FAQ results. The Teams admin-center route blocks the Teams app, not the equivalent cross-endpoint tenant switch.
